title: Rename Variable

solutions.title: Names earned by working out the arithmetic first
solutions.tradeoff: A rename cannot change behaviour, which cuts both ways: the suite can never break on a bad rename, so it can never confirm a good one either. Two identifiers could swap names and every test would still pass - the only backstop is a reader who checks the name against the formula, not against the old name's suggestion.

reviewFocus: Does each renamed identifier match what the arithmetic actually computes, or what its old single-letter name merely suggested it might be - check the replacement for `t` against the variance formula, not against the word "time"?

Could any two of the renamed identifiers swap places and still compile and pass the suite? If so, their meanings need to be verified independently - a self-consistent swap is invisible to every command in this repository.
Did the reduce callback's own parameters get renamed, or only the `const` declarations? Rename Variable covers a function's parameters as much as its locals.

Is `meanPace` computed inline a second time, or does it call the shared `averagePaceSecondsPerKm` that already exists two functions away? A rename that reveals a duplicate computation is a second finding, not a distraction from this one.

Would a plausible-sounding but wrong name (`variance` for the mean-of-squares term, say) have survived a skim? That near-miss is the one worth discussing, not the single-letter names - those fail on sight.
